newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-TESTS ON YANKEES' RHP CONE REVEAL MILD TENDINITIS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-TESTS ON YANKEES' RHP CONE REVEAL MILD TENDINITIS.

text.p: The New York Yankees received some encouraging news Monday when extensive tests on ace right-hander David Cone revealed only mild tendinitis in his right shoulder.
Cone pitched just one inning Sunday against the Texas Rangers before leaving with tightness in his shoulder near the area of an aneurysm he had surgically removed last year.
Team physician Dr. Stuart Hershon and Dr. George Todd said Monday's tests showed no vascular problem and no recurrence of the aneurysm. The team said Cone would be treated "conservatively."
The Yankees begin a West Coast road trip in Anaheim Tuesday and Cone will miss at least one start.
Cone retired the first two batters in the first inning Sunday, but then struggled with his location. He threw just 21 pitches before leaving the game.
The 34-year-old Cone is 12-6 in 26 starts this season. Last season, Cone made a successful return following surgery to remove an aneurysm in his pitching arm.

He was 4-1 before the aneurysm was diognosed. He came back September 2 to pitch seven no-hit innings and combined with Mariano Rivera on a one-hit shutout. Cone went 3-1 with a 3.94 ERA in September and helped the Yankees win the World Series.
The 12-year veteran has a lifetime record of 148-86 in 325 games with Kansas City, the New York Mets, Toronto and the Yankees.
